introHtml:
If you need mobile home skirting in Ocala, you've probably got one of three problems: panels blown loose from a summer storm, a park manager letter about compliance, or a home that just looks tired from the street. Ocala Level Pros handles all three. We install and repair vinyl and rigid-foam skirting across Marion, Sumter, and Citrus counties, and we do it with the ventilation and pest sealing that Florida's climate demands.

Skirting isn't just cosmetic. It keeps animals out from under your home, protects your vapor barrier and plumbing from the elements, and it's one of the first things an appraiser or buyer notices. A full install runs $1,200 to $3,500 depending on your home's size and the material you pick. Repairs usually land between $250 and $800. Call (352) 247-3105 and we'll give you a free written estimate with real numbers, not a range that doubles once we show up.

sections.heading: Vinyl vs. Rigid-Foam Skirting: What Works in Central Florida
sections.html:
Vinyl skirting is the workhorse around here. It's the cheapest way to fully enclose a home, usually landing at the lower end of the $1,200 to $3,500 install range for a single-wide. The trade-off is durability. Vinyl gets brittle in the Florida sun over the years, and a hard gust or a weed trimmer can crack a panel. The good news is that replacing one vinyl panel is a quick, cheap fix.

Rigid-foam skirting costs more, typically the middle to upper end of that range, but it earns the difference. The panels are thicker, they interlock, and they shrug off wind that would strip vinyl. They also insulate the crawl space, which helps with floor temperatures and keeps your under-home plumbing happier in a cold snap. If you're planning to stay in the home ten years or more, foam usually pencils out.

Either way, the install quality matters more than the material. Skirting attached to a home that isn't sitting level will bow, gap, and pull loose within a season. If your doors stick or your floors slope, it's worth having us check the piers first. We handle mobile home leveling in Ocala too, and doing it before the skirting goes on saves you from paying twice.

sections.heading: Ventilation and Pest Exclusion Done Right
sections.html:
Skirting has two jobs that fight each other: keep critters out, let air through. Florida code calls for about 1 square foot of net vent area for every 150 square feet of under-home space, and that ratio exists because a sealed, unvented crawl space in our humidity becomes a mold and rot factory. We've pulled skirting off homes where the previous installer skipped vents entirely, and the damage underneath cost far more than the skirting ever did.

On the pest side, the weak points are always the same: the ground track, the panel-to-panel joints, and the access door. We set the track into the ground properly, seal the seams, and install an access panel that actually latches. Here's what that keeps out from under your home:

  • Rats and mice that chew wiring and insulation
  • Armadillos that dig under piers and disturb your foundation pads
  • Snakes and raccoons looking for a dry, shaded den
  • Standing moisture that wrecks your vapor barrier and floor joists

Good vents come with rodent screens built in, so you don't have to choose between airflow and pest protection. We use them as standard, not as an upsell.

sections.heading: Hurricane-Season Skirting Repairs
sections.html:
Every June through November we get the same calls: a storm rolled through Ocala, Silver Springs, or Summerfield overnight and now there's skirting laying in the yard. Wind gets a finger under one loose panel and unzips a whole wall of it. Most of these repairs run $250 to $800 depending on how many panels and how much track we're replacing, and if your skirting is a common vinyl profile we can usually match it closely enough that you won't spot the repair from the street.

The practical move is to fix small problems before storm season, not after. A single loose panel in May is a $250 repair. That same panel in August is the starting point for a wall of missing skirting, wet insulation, and a crawl space full of debris. While we're under there, it's also smart to have your tie-downs and anchors checked, since loose straps and loose skirting tend to show up together on older homes.

If you're up against an insurance deadline or a pre-closing inspection, we run a 24/7 emergency line at (352) 247-3105. We can document the damage, quote the repair in writing, and get it scheduled fast.

sections.heading: Park Rules, Resale Value, and What Skirting Costs
sections.html:
If you live in one of the 55+ communities around Ocala, Belleview, or Lady Lake, your park probably has written skirting standards: approved materials, approved colors, sometimes a deadline to fix visible damage. Those letters from the park office aren't optional, and some parks fine residents who let it slide. We've worked in plenty of these communities, so tell us which park you're in and we'll install to their spec the first time. That's one inspection you pass without a second visit.

Skirting also punches above its weight at resale. It's the biggest visual surface on the home besides the roof, and buyers read cracked, gapped, or mismatched skirting as a sign the whole home was neglected. For a $1,200 to $3,500 investment, new skirting changes how the home shows more than almost anything else you can do outside. Pair it with a quick landscaping cleanup along the skirting line and the home looks years newer. We see this pay off in resale-heavy areas like Belleview and Summerfield all the time.

Here's how pricing typically breaks down:

  • Full vinyl install, single-wide: roughly $1,200 to $2,000
  • Full vinyl install, double-wide: roughly $1,800 to $2,800
  • Rigid-foam install: roughly $2,200 to $3,500 depending on home size
  • Repairs: $250 to $800 for most panel and track work

Every job starts with a free written estimate. If the numbers change once we're on site, you'll know why before any work starts. Curious how skirting fits into the bigger picture of home costs? Our leveling cost guide covers what the rest of the under-home work runs.

faq.q: How much does mobile home skirting cost in Ocala?
faq.a: A full install runs $1,200 to $3,500 depending on your home's size and material. Vinyl on a single-wide sits at the low end, around $1,200 to $2,000, while rigid-foam on a double-wide can reach $3,500. Repairs are much cheaper, typically $250 to $800. We give free written estimates so you have the exact number before we start.

faq.q: Which is better for Florida: vinyl or rigid-foam skirting?
faq.a: Vinyl costs less and individual panels are cheap to replace, but it gets brittle after years of Florida sun. Rigid-foam costs roughly 30 to 50 percent more, handles wind better, and insulates the space under your home. If you plan to stay put for a decade, foam usually wins. If budget is tight or park rules require a specific look, vinyl does the job fine.

faq.q: Does skirting need vents in Florida?
faq.a: Yes. The standard is about 1 square foot of net vent area per 150 square feet of crawl space, spread around the perimeter so air actually moves through. Skipping vents in our humidity leads to condensation, mold, and rotted floor joists that cost far more than the skirting did. We calculate the vent count for your specific home and use vents with built-in rodent screens.

faq.q: My park sent a letter about my skirting. Can you help me meet their rules?
faq.a: Yes, this is common in 55+ communities around Ocala, Belleview, and Lady Lake. Parks often specify approved materials, colors, and a repair deadline. Tell us which community you're in when you call (352) 247-3105 and we'll match their written standards. Most compliance repairs land in the $250 to $800 range unless the whole run needs replacement.

faq.q: How fast can you repair storm-damaged skirting?
faq.a: During hurricane season we prioritize storm calls, and most repairs are done in a single visit once materials are matched. Typical storm repairs run $250 to $800 for panels and track. If you're facing an insurance deadline or a pre-closing inspection, our 24/7 emergency line at (352) 247-3105 gets you documentation and a written quote fast.
